query: Starting from a W–Cu composite containing W particles or interconnected W ligaments within a Cu matrix, what single intervention could overcome phase separation and interfacial void formation, thereby improving thermal conductivity relative to the untreated composite under heat-transfer and irradiation conditions relevant to joints between W-based plasma-facing materials and Cu-based cooling components? Formulate one hypothesis that states the intervention, the proposed mechanism, the predicted comparative outcome, the applicable processing and service boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a high-temperature solid-state diffusion bonding process to the W–Cu composite, followed by controlled cooling, will reduce phase separation and interfacial void formation, thereby improving thermal conductivity under heat-transfer and irradiation conditions relevant to W/Cu joints.
generation.material_initial_state: W–Cu composite containing W particles or interconnected W ligaments within a Cu matrix, with typical phase separation and interfacial voids.
generation.intervention: High-temperature solid-state diffusion bonding, followed by controlled cooling.
generation.conditions: Processing at temperatures above the Cu melting point but below W melting point, under inert atmosphere; service under heat-transfer and irradiation relevant to plasma-facing joints.
generation.structural_mediator: Enhanced interfacial bonding and reduced voids at W–Cu interfaces.
generation.mechanism: Diffusion bonding promotes atomic intermixing at the W–Cu interface, healing voids and reducing phase separation, resulting in improved interface continuity and reduced thermal resistance.
generation.predicted_outcome: Thermal conductivity of the treated composite will be measurably higher than the untreated composite under relevant heat-transfer and irradiation conditions.
generation.baseline: Untreated W–Cu composite with typical phase separation and interfacial voids.
generation.boundary: Applicable to W–Cu composites processed by solid-state diffusion bonding at temperatures below W melting point; not applicable if excessive melting or grain growth occurs.
generation.uncertainty: No direct prior evidence supplied; effect size and durability under irradiation are uncertain.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of W–Cu composites: one untreated, one subjected to high-temperature solid-state diffusion bonding and controlled cooling. Expose both to heat-transfer and irradiation conditions relevant to plasma-facing joints. Measure thermal conductivity and inspect interfaces for voids and phase separation.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the treated composite does not show reduced interfacial voids and phase separation, or if its thermal conductivity is not higher than the untreated composite under relevant conditions, the hypothesis is falsified.
